sources.entry: LockDown - Open-source tool for El Capitan that audits and remediates security configuration settings. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/lockdown) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Lockdown
summary.one_liner: Lockdown is a macOS/OS X GUI wrapper around Summit Route's open-source osxlockdown tool that audits and hardens system security configuration settings.
use_cases: Audit a Mac's security configuration without making changes
Harden an OS X system to reduce its attack surface
Enable recommended security features like the firewall
Disable optional features such as AirDrop for security
Track a security pass rate score before and after fixes
summary.what_it_does: Lockdown is a graphical wrapper over the open-source osxlockdown tool, giving a checkbox list of security configuration rules. Users can toggle individual rules on or off in the UI. The 'audit' button checks the system and reports PASSED or FAILED for each rule plus an overall pass rate, without changing anything. The 'fix' button applies the enabled rules, which may disable some functionality. The app requires an administrator password via a standard authorization prompt, and it verifies itself and the osxlockdown components cryptographically.
notable: Graphical UI wrapper over Summit Route's osxlockdown, which is open source
Audit mode reports PASSED/FAILED per rule and a final pass rate without changing the system
Individual rules can be toggled off via checkboxes
Cryptographic self-verification of Lockdown and osxlockdown components
caveats: Fix mode makes system changes that may disable functionality; the author advises backing up first
Some commands may fail in certain scenarios, with failure logic residing in osxlockdown
Page lists the version as designed for El Capitan (OS X 10.11) per the listing, and the page describes it as OS X software, so newer macOS compatibility is not stated
